One question per page except: p08 has no question number (option (d) graph of Q7, continued from p07) and p13 has no question number (options (c) and (d) of Q11, continued from p12). Stem figures: Q2 pedigree (p02), Q15 O2 dissociation curves (p17). Picture options: Q7 (p07 a-c, p08 d), Q11 (p12 a-b, p13 c-d). Q3 and Q8 match tables are printed as pictures; typed as pipe tables. Q9's cross scheme is typed in the stem (no figure needed).

rows.text:
What will be the sequence of RNA synthesized using the following DNA template strand?

5'-GTCTAGGCTTCTC-3'

The following pedigree diagram shows the inheritance of a rare genetic disorder (filled shapes depict affected individuals).

Which of the following is the most likely pattern of inheritance of the disorder?

figure.note: Four-generation pedigree (squares = males, circles = females, filled = affected). Generation I: affected female mated with unaffected male. Their children (generation II, left to right): affected female (mated with an unaffected male), unaffected male, unaffected female, affected male (mated with an unaffected female). Children of the affected generation-II female and unaffected male (left to right): affected male (mated with an unaffected female), affected female, unaffected male, unaffected female. Children of the affected generation-II male and unaffected female (left to right): unaffected male, affected female, unaffected male. Generation IV, children of the affected generation-III male and unaffected female (left to right): unaffected male, affected female, affected female, unaffected male.

rows.text:
Match the list of conditions (Column I) with the list of affected physiological processes (Column II).

| | Column I | | Column II |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | Allergy | i | Excess secretion of growth hormone |
| Q | Uremia | ii | Exaggerated immune response to environmental substances |
| R | Myasthenia gravis | iii | Autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction |
| S | Acromegaly | iv | Malfunctioning of kidneys which can lead to urea accumulation in the blood |

Which of the following combinations is correct?
rows._flag: Column I mixes chapters (allergy and myasthenia gravis are immune disorders; uremia is excretory; acromegaly is endocrine). Filed under Human Health and Disease / Immunity as the closest single fit.

rows.text: Which of the following proteins plays a direct role in muscle contraction?
Which of the following is NOT derived from the epidermal cell layer in plants?
Which of the following statements about meiosis in sexually reproducing plants is INCORRECT?
options: The end products of meiosis II are haploid gametes.
The four products of meiosis are genetically different.
Meiotic recombination takes place in both males and females.
In most flowering plants, only one of the four products of meiosis survives in females.

rows.text: Which of the following graphs represents the correct relationship between light intensity (X-axis) and the rate of photosynthesis (Y-axis)?
options: Graph of Y against X: rising from the origin almost linearly, then levelling off into a flat plateau
Graph of Y against X: S-shaped curve, flat near the origin, then rising steeply, then a flat plateau
Graph of Y against X: rising from the origin to a peak, then falling back to the X-axis
Graph of Y against X: a straight line rising from the origin

Two species of a flowering plant, P (\(2n = 20\) chromosomes) and Q (\(2n = 30\) chromosomes) are reciprocally crossed with each other as male or female as shown below to produce F1 seeds.

♀ Plant P \(\times\) ♂ Plant Q \(\longrightarrow\) F1 seeds (R)

♀ Plant Q \(\times\) ♂ Plant P \(\longrightarrow\) F1 seeds (S)

Which of the following seed tissues from both the F1 seeds (R and S) will have the same chromosome numbers?
Which of the following is routinely performed to detect typhoid?

Which of the following plasmid vectors can be used for cloning of a gene, with restriction enzymes BamHI and EcoRI, and ampicillin-containing nutrient agar for selection?

[Ori and Amp\(^{R}\) represent origin of replication and gene for ampicillin resistance, respectively.]
options: Circular plasmid vector with Ori and Amp\(^{R}\); EcoRI and BamHI sites both on the circle, away from Ori and Amp\(^{R}\)
Circular plasmid vector with Ori and Amp\(^{R}\); BamHI site on the circle just beside the end of Amp\(^{R}\), EcoRI site elsewhere on the circle
Circular plasmid vector with Ori and Amp\(^{R}\); BamHI site on the circle just beside Ori, EcoRI site elsewhere on the circle
Circular plasmid vector with Ori and Amp\(^{R}\); BamHI site marked on Ori itself, EcoRI site elsewhere on the circle

rows.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
rows.text: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is used to amplify a gene of interest (GOI). If, after 30 cycles of PCR, 1 billion copies of GOI are produced, approximately how many copies of GOI were present at the end of the \(20^{th}\) cycle?

A population with \(\mathrm{N} = 400\) individuals increases in numbers till it reaches an asymptote at \(\mathrm{K} = 500\) individuals, K being the carrying capacity. Assuming the intrinsic rate of natural increase (r) to be 0.01, what would be the population growth rate (dN/dt)?
Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Hemichordata is not considered as a chordate sub-phylum, and possesses a proto-notochord called stomochord.
Hemichordata is a sub-phylum under Chordata and possesses a proto-notochord called stomochord.
Hemichordata is a sub-phylum under Chordata and possesses a proper notochord and gill slits like chordates.
Hemichordata is not considered as a chordate sub-phylum because it possesses a water vascular system.

rows.text: Which of the following statements is correct about the oxygen \(\mathrm{(O_2)}\) dissociation curves (**A** and **C**) relative to curve **B**?

figure.note: Y-axis '% O2 saturation of Haemoglobin' (arrow up), X-axis 'pO2' (arrow right). Three sigmoid curves from the origin, all meeting at the same plateau at top right: A (solid black, leftmost), B (red, middle), C (dashed, rightmost).

options: Curve **A** represents favourable \(\mathrm{O_2}\) association with haemoglobin at low \(\mathrm{[H^+]}\).
Curve **C** represents favourable \(\mathrm{O_2}\) association with haemoglobin at low \(\mathrm{pCO_2}\).
Curve **A** represents favourable \(\mathrm{O_2}\) association with haemoglobin at low pH.
Curve **C** represents favourable \(\mathrm{O_2}\) association with haemoglobin at high \(\mathrm{pO_2}\).
